Sovereignty integration / Edition 05

A parallel control layer. Explicit joins.

Table defaults establish the contract. Business keys and context determine which rows may cross.

The two schemas meet at stable identities

Schema / tablePurposeJoin contract

sovereignty.table_ruleNarrowing table defaultowner + registered table
sovereignty.scopeParty or relationship authority, grants, purpose and epochsowner + root_type + root_id
sovereignty.bindingMany-to-many scope membershipowner + scope + resource_type + resource_id
sovereignty.resource_ruleShared-resource geographic/profile constraintsowner + resource_type + resource_id
sovereignty.outbox / audit / command_receiptAtomic export intent and business evidencesource transaction + scope + request ID
projection.* / manifest / inboxApproved recipient graph and deduplicationowner + scope + destination + row ID

Resolve rules by intersection

01Table contract

Registered columns and default mode, generic verified OPA bundle.

02Scope policy

03Resource rules

04Business context

05Connected manifest

Remove withheld fields and dependency orphans; commit atomically at recipient.

Why a sidecar is not zero integration

The operational writer calls a sovereignty hook within its existing database transaction. The hook registers new business resources, resolves affected scopes, advances versions and appends export intents. It does not call a remote policy service while holding the transaction. Every writer—including bulk import and future maintenance jobs—must follow this contract or be denied write credentials. A raw changefeed alone cannot infer relationship membership, contextual consent or an atomic multi-table view.

The polymorphic binding points to a typed resource registry and is checked by the application against the actual business table. The database enforces owner-aware parent references and scope keys, but cannot by itself prove that an arbitrary resource_type/resource_id pair exists in its named table. Production needs registry integrity checks and a fail-closed path for unregistered mutations.

Policy precedence examples

Table defaultKey/context restrictionResult
party: global minimumParty P2 excludes USNo P2 identifier in US.
relationship: policy federationRelationship R1 excludes USA global party never imports R1 into US.
contact_info: relationship policyR1 contact grant + EMAIL consent; PHONE has no consentEMAIL only in R1 projection.
product_holding: relationship policyHolding H1 classified RESTRICTEDH1 and dependent classification/alternate rows withheld.
contact_info: owner onlyR1 has a contact entitlementNo contact export; grant cannot override table restriction.

Safe read and removal semantics

data_version tracks ordinary business freshness. decision_revision changes on consent/classification. policy_generation changes on table/key controls. placement_version binds the recipient store. The harness checks current authority before serving a stored graph; mismatched authorisation or placement revisions block reads until reconciliation. Previously authorised data can remain physically present while ingress is paused, which the UI reports separately from access. Live projection removal does not certify audit, inbox, backup or legal-hold erasure.

Source-side denial is deliberate

A never-authorised destination receives no customer-specific denial record or tombstone. A previously authorised destination may retain a governed receipt after removing its payload so replayed old work cannot resurrect a copy. Rule bundles can be generic and global; customer-linked control facts remain subject to residency.

Extend the v3 operational PoC, preserving 30 legal entities and three independent single-node store models. Business data is normalized across 12 tables; sovereignty policies live in parallel control tables. A separate party scope exports only id/global_party_id/party_type; relationship scopes export connected whitelisted graphs. Global distribution still needs grants and approved geography; deny overrides. Do not infer relationship access from a global party, common store or shared identity. Keep the single local transaction and asynchronous destination acknowledgement distinct. The hosted UI is a labelled browser simulation. The unified Docker/CockroachDB/OPA suite and live Chromium generator/migration walkthrough passed. Database crash boundaries, accessibility and pilot load remain separate gates. Use synthetic data only. Deliver bounded adapters, actual migrations, meaningful invariant tests and honest run results.

Implement a reusable SovereigntyHook on the same local unit of work as business mutations. Resolve table registry, scopes and hard resource restrictions from trusted state. OPA must default-deny missing datasets/facts. Build a dependency-closed manifest and enforce recipient foreign keys, idempotent inbox and monotonically fenced versions. Test cross-scope contamination, table/key narrowing, consent per relationship/channel, missing parents and stale replay. Add direct-writer controls before claiming parallel sovereignty is complete.
